name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia with t(8;21)(q22;q22) Translocation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of t(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation confirmed by cytogenetic or molecular testing
Bone marrow or peripheral blood blasts ≥20%
Myeloblasts with Auer rods and dysplastic granulocytic lineage
Expression of myeloid markers CD13, CD33, and CD34 with aberrant expression of CD19

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of t(8;21)(q22;q22) translocation with ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood and characteristic morphologic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation of RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion gene is diagnostic; immunophenotyping supports diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Auer rods in myeloblasts
pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive cytoplasmic inclusions seen on bone marrow smear
searchTerms: rod-shaped inclusions in immature white cells
Auer rods seen in blood cells

pathognomonic.symptomName: RUNX1-RUNX1T1 fusion gene detected by molecular testing
pathognomonic.notes: Specific genetic hallmark of this AML subtype

searchTerms: pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells

common.symptomName: Thrombocytopenia leading to easy bruising and petechiae
searchTerms: low platelets causing bruises and spots
easy bruising with small red dots
petechiae and bleeding from low platelets
bleeding under skin due to thrombocytopenia

common.notes: Increased susceptibility to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: infections due to low white cells

common.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with myeloblast proliferation
searchTerms: bone marrow with too many immature blasts
excess immature blood cells in marrow

occasional.notes: Often related to infection or disease activity
Less common in this AML subtype

rare.notes: Due to high blast counts causing microvascular occlusion
searchTerms: lung problems from blood cell buildup

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing myeloblasts with Auer rods
imaging: Chest X-ray may show infiltrates if leukostasis or infection present
Ultrasound or CT may reveal hepatosplenomegaly
other: Immunophenotyping showing CD13+, CD33+, CD34+, CD19+ aberrant expression
Coagulation profile to assess for DIC

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of inv(16)(p13q22) or t(16;16) translocation
Eosinophilia in peripheral blood and bone marrow
Lymphoid rather than myeloid blast immunophenotype

redFlags: Signs of leukostasis such as respiratory distress or neurological deficits
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Döhner H, et al. Diagnosis and management of AML in adults: 2017 ELN recommendations from an international expert panel. Blood. 2017.
